In a landscape stitched with rivers and low-lying coasts, the sea simply rose and moved inland, showing how geography and poverty can turn weather into catastrophe.

episode.description: An analogy between diving, one of Gaia's great passions, and the act of immersing in life itself. A reflection on what happens when we go below the surface: when we let ourselves be fully present. From moments of calm suspension to warm, rhythmic flow, the selection moves like water — fluid, organic, and alive. An invitation to slow down, listen deeper, and float.

queue.fact_text: On May 25, 1935, Jesse Owens broke three world records and tied a fourth in just 45 minutes at the Big Ten Championships in Ann Arbor—an athletic explosion often called the greatest 45 minutes in sports. On a sore back and cinder track, he turned an ordinary meet into a legend of speed and grace.

episode.title: Morning Drops #01 - Timeless Legacy
episode.description: Gaia guides us through timeless music to start the morning with the right foot! The first episode of the Morning Drops series — classic sounds that never fade.
songs: Roberta Flack - Killing me softly with his song

queue.match_reason: Owens’ record-shattering performance is a human 'timeless legacy,' fitting an episode celebrating classic works that continue to inspire across generations.

queue.fact_text: The comic opera H.M.S. Pinafore premiered in London on May 25, 1878, launching Gilbert and Sullivan into international fame. Beneath its cheerful melodies and seaside antics, the show quietly poked fun at class, bureaucracy, and naval tradition, proving that catchy tunes and social satire make a powerful duet.

episode.title: Morning Drops #38 - History of Flamenco
episode.description: A special journey into the history of Flamenco, guided by Yasmin and her guest Almudena from Madrid, Spain. Exploring the roots and evolution of this emotionally raw and culturally rich tradition, from its early vocal origins and Andalusian influences, through its transformation on stage and screen, to its modern reinventions by iconic Spanish artists.
songs: La Niña de los Peines - Al Gurugú
Paco de Lucía - Entre dos aguas

queue.match_reason: A witty, 19th‑century English comic opera and a deep dive into Flamenco are both about the evolution of theatrical, emotionally charged musical traditions that moved from niche stages to global culture.

queue.fact_text: On May 25, 1933, Disney’s animated short Three Little Pigs premiered, introducing the hit song "Who’s Afraid of the Big Bad Wolf?" to Depression-era audiences. The film’s playful defiance of danger turned a children’s tale into an unofficial anthem of resilience during hard economic times.

episode.title: Morning Drops #34 - Soul Sisters
episode.description: A tribute to four iconic voices — women who have shaped the way we listen, feel, and move. Each track carries a different kind of presence: one that holds you, one that questions, one that grounds, and one that lets go. An energy that is soulful, raw, and unapologetically feminine.
songs: Grace Jones - Walking in the Rain
Aretha Franklin - A Rose Is Still a Rose

queue.match_reason: A simple cartoon song became an anthem of emotional strength; this lines up with an episode celebrating powerful voices who sing about facing fear and standing tall in their own way.

queue.fact_text: On May 25, 1977, Star Wars opened in U.S. theaters, unexpectedly launching one of the most influential space sagas in cinema. Audiences stepped into a galaxy where myth and futurism danced together, and sound design—from lightsabers to John Williams’ score—became as iconic as the visuals.

episode.title: Morning Drops #30 - Star Treatment
episode.description: A celebration of change and transformation. Gaia traces the evolution of Arctic Monkeys - from raw energy to cinematic sound - reflecting on how artists, and all of us, grow and change through time. A journey through courage, curiosity, and the beauty of slowing down.
songs: Arctic Monkeys - There’d Better Be a Mirrorball

queue.match_reason: The birth of the Star Wars universe and an episode titled 'Star Treatment' both center on cinematic worlds, transformation, and turning ordinary beginnings into sprawling sagas.

queue.fact_text: On May 25, 2011, Oprah Winfrey aired the final episode of The Oprah Winfrey Show, closing a 25-year run that turned daytime television into a space for confessions, book clubs, and cultural shifts. Her studio couch became a global confessional where private stories regularly rippled through public life.

episode.title: Morning Drops #37 - Happy Birthday Gaia
episode.description: A special Morning Drop to celebrate Gaia's birthday and the first anniversary of Sedna FM. A journey through friendship, music, and voice messages from the people who've known her longest. From street dance classes in Milan to creative adventures in London, a tribute to growing up together and showing up for each other.
songs: The Mighty Tiny & The Many Few - Good Foot

queue.match_reason: A long-running, intimate talk show ending and a birthday-anniversary radio episode both celebrate the power of personal storytelling, community, and looking back on years of shared growth.

queue.fact_text: On May 25, 1940, the German 2nd Panzer Division completed the capture of Boulogne-sur-Mer, ending the Battle of Boulogne in World War II. The fall of this coastal port tightened the noose around Allied forces retreating toward Dunkirk, compressing entire armies into a shrinking pocket of sand and sea.

episode.title: Morning Drops #49 - Rage Against The Machine
episode.description:
In this Morning Drop, Yasmin revisits the story of Rage Against the Machine — a band born in tension, shaped by conviction, and remembered for moments that blurred the line between stage and protest.
From early Los Angeles unrest to Wall Street performances, this episode moves through rupture, resistance, and legacy — carried by songs that still feel urgent today.
Listen closely.
songs: Rage Against the Machine - Killing in the Name
Rage Against the Machine - Without a Face
Rage Against the Machine - Guerrilla Radio
Rage Against the Machine - Sleep Now in the Fire

queue.match_reason: A grim chapter of mechanized war and occupation pairs with an episode about a band who channels anger and politics into sound, confronting structures of power that wars are fought over.

queue.fact_text: The May Revolution reached its peak on May 25, 1810, when citizens of Buenos Aires forced the resignation of Viceroy Baltasar Hidalgo de Cisneros. That week of protests and assemblies cracked open Spanish colonial rule and lit the fuse for the Argentine War of Independence.

episode.title: Morning Drops #44 - Residente
episode.description:
In this edition of Morning Drops, Yasmin navigates the complex geography of René Pérez Joglar, known to the world as Residente. His story is not just a musical evolution; it is a timeline marked by resistance, lyrical obsession, and a relentless search for identity.

From the gated streets of Trujillo Alto to the global stage, we explore how a restless mind transformed into the voice of a generation. The selection moves through the textures of his life: hearing the raw energy of his early rebellion, the sharp precision of his political critique, and finally, the fragile silence of his most personal confessions.

It is a study in duality. We witness the rapper who dismantles giants and the son who misses his mother. It is a soundscape that proves that sometimes, the loudest revolution happens inside.

Mood: Raw, Revolutionary, Introspective, Honest
Music genre: Latin Alternative, Hip Hop, Urban, World

queue.match_reason: A Latin American revolution in Buenos Aires harmonizes with an episode about Residente, whose music is steeped in Latin American identity, resistance, and the politics of the Spanish-speaking world.

queue.fact_text: The Chuquisaca Revolution broke out on May 25, 1809, in what is now Sucre, Bolivia, as local elites and citizens rose up against the Spanish authorities. Though small in scale, the revolt is remembered as one of the sparks that ignited a continent-wide chain of independence movements.

episode.title: Morning Drops #13 - Demystifying Reggaeton
episode.description: Yasmin takes us on a journey through the real story of reggaeton — from its roots in Panama and Puerto Rico to its global evolution. Exploring the genre's history, influences, and cultural impact.
songs: Renato - Chica de los Ojos Café
B. F. Yaviah - Si Tu Quieres Fumar

queue.match_reason: An early independence revolt in Spanish America connects with an episode tracing a modern Latin genre born from marginalized voices and Caribbean resistance, both part of a long arc of cultural and political assertion.

queue.fact_text: On May 25, 1738, a treaty between Pennsylvania and Maryland helped end Cresap’s War, a surprisingly intense border conflict sparked by overlapping land claims. After years of raids, arrests, and disputed survey lines, the two colonies agreed to exchange prisoners and start formalizing the boundary that would eventually become part of the Mason–Dixon line.

episode.title: Morning Drops #39 - Moving Meditation
episode.description: An episode inspired by how travel helps us see more clearly. Stepping into new places opens the mind, shifts perspective. The music moves through balearic warmth, boogie grooves, world and latin-folk influences, and touches of new wave — a selection built to follow the quiet changes that happen when you're out of your usual rhythm.
songs: España Circo Este - Dormo poco e sogno molto
Talking Heads - This Must Be the Place (Naive Melody)

queue.match_reason: A territorial dispute resolved by redefining borders mirrors an episode about movement, shifting perspectives, and crossing lines—geographic and mental—to find calmer ground.

queue.fact_text: On May 25, 2008’s Martian touchdown and 2012’s Dragon rendezvous weren’t the first cosmic visitors to our skies—Halley’s Comet has been doing flybys for millennia. Ancient observers carefully recorded its passage even without knowing they were all watching the same traveler, unknowingly co-authoring one of humanity’s longest-running space logs.

episode.title: Morning Drops #14 - Slow Planet
episode.description: A pause. A quiet return to slower rhythms, sparked by a live set under the summer sky. A moment to breathe and settle into the week.

queue.match_reason: Halley’s slow, cyclical returns through our skies align with the episode’s invitation to inhabit a 'slow planet'—watching cosmic motion on a timescale larger than our own days.

queue.fact_text: Nature’s raw power marked May 25 more than once: while Udall, Kansas faced an F5 tornado in 1955, that same date in 1985 saw Bangladesh endure a deadly cyclone and storm surge. These twin anniversaries remind us that Earth’s atmosphere can shape destinies within a single night, from the Great Plains to the Bay of Bengal.

episode.title: Morning Drops #40 - Diving With Orcas
episode.description: Yasmin's friend Caroline takes us beyond the polar circle, into the Arctic waters of Norway, where orcas and humpback whales gather each winter. A personal journey shaped by a quiet obsession with orcas, from Patagonia to the icy fjords of the north. The soundscape moves gently between cinematic swells and soft, rhythmic pulses — echoing the cold light of Arctic mornings and the grace of underwater encounters.

queue.match_reason: Stories of extreme weather and ocean surges pair with an episode about powerful seas and marine giants, all shaped by the motion of water and the atmosphere.

queue.fact_text: From Buenos Aires in 1810 to Chuquisaca in 1809, the events of May 25 trace a map of Latin American uprisings against colonial rule. These local revolutions, born in plazas and council halls, would eventually ripple outward into new flags, new borders, and entirely new musical and cultural identities.

episode.title: Morning Drops #24 - The Rise Of Afrobeat
episode.description: An exploration of the rise of Afrobeat, tracing its roots and evolution as a genre that blends African rhythms with jazz, funk, and highlife. A celebration of the infectious energy and cultural significance of this influential musical movement.

queue.match_reason: Latin American independence movements and the rise of Afrobeat are both stories of regions reshaping their futures and exporting new rhythms of freedom to the world.

queue.fact_text: May 25 now carries layers of shared memory: daring climbs on Everest and Kangchenjunga, firsts in spaceflight, storms, revolutions, and even a certain galaxy far, far away. Taken together, the date reads like a collage of human risk-taking—scientific, artistic, political, and deeply personal.

episode.title: Sedna On The Go #02 - The Adventures of A Guitar by Ricardo Fiel
episode.description:
In this Sedna on the Go, Yasmin sits down with Ricardo Fiel in a small café in front of the beach in Lisbon. A spontaneous conversation, recorded with waves, coffee cups, and the occasional passer-by in the background.

Ricardo, born and raised, in portugal, leads a life worth discovering. By day, he moves through the world of tech. But there is another side. A side of a rockstar, of full stadiums and after parties! A side we are happy to share with you in this episode

Listen slowly, and let the place come through with him.

queue.match_reason: A day packed with diverse adventures—from mountains to Mars—sits well with a conversational episode about a life lived between tech and rock stages, collecting stories and sounds along the way.

published.fact_text: On May 25, 2008, NASA’s Phoenix lander touched down in the Martian region known as Green Valley and gently scooped into alien soil in search of ice and possible habitats for microscopic life. Designed to operate in the frigid Martian arctic, Phoenix confirmed the presence of water ice just below the surface, turning a patch of red desert into one of the most scientifically important gardens in the Solar System.

episode.title: Morning Drops #03 - Space Shift
episode.description: Gaia invites you to shift your mindset with a simple yet powerful reflection: What if we saw emptiness not as a void but as space to create? An energising and feel-good selection of tracks, the perfect way to ease into your day and set the tone for the week ahead.

The Strokes - You Only Live Once

published.match_reason: Phoenix turned the 'emptiness' of Martian arctic plains into a space for discovery, echoing the episode’s theme of reimagining emptiness as room to create and explore.

published.fact_text: In 2012, the uncrewed SpaceX Dragon 1 capsule became the first commercial spacecraft to rendezvous and berth with the International Space Station. This quietly marked a turning point in spaceflight, as access to orbit began shifting from the realm of nation-states to collaborations between agencies and private innovators.

episode.title: Sedna FM #02 - Destination Sedna

published.fact_text: On May 25, 1961, John F. Kennedy stood before the U.S. Congress and proposed a goal that sounded almost impossible: landing a human on the Moon and returning them safely to Earth before the decade ended. This single speech lit the fuse for the Apollo program and compressed an era of experimentation, risk, and engineering brilliance into less than ten years.

episode.title: Morning Drops #48 - Cosmic Monday
episode.description:
Cosmic Monday is a Morning Drops episode built around four Italian dance records, tracing how disco rhythms slowly became electronic language.
Gaia moves through four tracks like chapters: groove first, then machines, then that bright, futuristic feeling you only get when the bassline is doing the talking. It's not nostalgia, exactly. It's more like returning to a sound that still works — especially on mornings when you need a little extra energy, but you don't want anything aggressive.
Take it as a slow transmission. Let it carry you into the day.
songs: Giovanotti Mondani Meccanici - Don't Ask Me Why

published.match_reason: A moonshot speech that launched humans toward the cosmos pairs with an episode steeped in 'cosmic' dance energy and futuristic electronic textures.

published.fact_text: The first recorded perihelion passage of Halley’s Comet was noted in 240 BCE, centuries before anyone knew it was the same visitor returning again and again. Only much later did astronomers recognize its pattern, turning ghostly omens into a predictable, clocklike traveler in the night sky.

episode.title: Evening Flows #00 - Introduction to evening flows
episode.description:
Sedna FM introduces a new format: Evening Flow, where you can enjoy curated music sets from selectors, DJs, and artists.

Each mix is an invitation to drift beyond the expected. A space where hidden gems from personal archives come to light, where sound speaks its own language. There are no rules here, no patterns to follow. Just the steady unfolding of a mood, a texture, a journey shaped by feeling.

Let the music lead the way - enjoy the trip!

published.match_reason: Halley’s Comet is a recurring celestial visitor that reshaped how we see the night; a format-launching 'evening flow' mirrors the idea of a new recurring journey through the dark, guided only by patterns of light and sound.

published.fact_text: Explorer 32, launched on May 25, 1966, was a satellite sent into a highly elliptical orbit to probe Earth’s upper atmosphere. By repeatedly diving through the rarefied air hundreds of kilometers up, it helped scientists understand how our planet’s thin outer envelope swells and shrinks with the Sun’s moods.

episode.title: Morning Drops #25 - A Trip-Hop Journey

From Bristol's early experiments with Massive Attack and Tricky, to DJ Shadow's cinematic sampling in California, and Thievery Corporation's global downtempo grooves in Washington D.C. — exploring how this genre blurred boundaries and reshaped electronic music.
songs: Tricky - Hell Is Round the Corner
DJ Shadow - Midnight in a Perfect World

published.match_reason: Explorer 32’s looping path through the atmosphere parallels the episode’s 'journey' structure, drifting through layered, atmospheric trip-hop much like a satellite coasting through Earth’s upper air.

published.fact_text: In 1955, the British Kangchenjunga expedition achieved the first ascent of the world’s third-highest mountain. Out of respect for local beliefs that the summit was sacred, the climbers famously stopped just a few feet below the true top, standing at the edge of achievement without fully claiming it.

episode.title: Morning Drops #22 - Sicilians On The Dolomites
episode.description: Hosted by Yasmin, a musical journey inspired by the mountains. Joined by two special guests, exploring the tracks they've chosen, hearing the stories behind their picks, and discovering the personal memories each song brings to life — a blend of music, voices, and landscapes you can hear.
songs: Florian Pellissier Quintet - Coup de foudre à Thessalonique
Lucio Dalla & Francesco De Gregori - Ma come fanno i marinai

published.match_reason: A story of climbing into sacred heights fits an episode woven around mountain landscapes, where music and memory trace ridgelines and quiet acts of respect for nature.

published.fact_text: On May 25, 2001, Erik Weihenmayer became the first blind person to reach the summit of Mount Everest. Guided by sound, touch, and trust in his team, he transformed the world’s highest peak from a purely visual symbol into a testament to human adaptability and resilience.

episode.title: Morning Drops #42 - The Joy Of Learning
episode.description:
Hosted by Yasmin, this Morning Drop explores learning as a lifelong process, focusing on persistence, repetition, and the emotional landscape that comes with challenging oneself over time.

Through personal stories and scientific insights, the episode looks at how learning reshapes the brain, generates joy through effort, and why progress often arrives after confusion and frustration. It reflects on the so-called delayed pleasure effect, the role of dopamine in motivation, and how curiosity and learning support long-term wellbeing.

The episode also questions our cultural relationship with failure and invites a softer, more realistic approach to learning, one that accepts mistakes as part of growth and sees persistence as a quiet form of strength.

Mood: reflective, grounded, quietly hopeful
Music genre: alternative rock, hip hop, electronic, neo-soul, drill

A space to listen slowly and stay with the process.

published.match_reason: Weihenmayer’s ascent is a masterclass in perseverance and re-learning how to navigate the world, mirroring the episode’s focus on persistence, frustration, and the joy that comes after long effort.

published.fact_text: On May 25, 1953, KUHT in Houston became the first public television station in the United States, broadcasting educational content from a university campus. Long before online courses, it used the airwaves to turn living rooms into classrooms and cities into shared lecture halls.

episode.title: Sedna FM #01 - November Bomb

published.match_reason: The first public TV station and the first Sedna FM episode both mark humble beginnings of new broadcast spaces focused on sharing knowledge, stories, and community through media.

published.fact_text: Also on that same day in 1953, the United States fired a 280 mm nuclear shell during the Upshot–Knothole Grable test at the Nevada Test Site—the only time a nuclear artillery round has been detonated. The explosion turned a single cannon shot into a blinding, city-sized burst of energy, forever blurring the line between battlefield tactics and apocalyptic power.

published.match_reason: A nuclear artillery blast is the ultimate 'electric shock' to the planet; the episode’s title and high-voltage guitar energy resonate with the raw, dangerous power unleashed in that test.

published.fact_text: On May 25, 1955, a violent nighttime F5 tornado struck Udall, Kansas, killing 80 people in the deadliest tornado in the state’s history. With little warning and no modern radar alerts, the storm arrived as an invisible wall of wind and debris, turning a quiet prairie town into a cautionary tale about nature’s sudden extremes.

The musical selection mirrors this journey, moving from the orchestral depth of changing seasons into the golden warmth of psychedelic soul. It recalls memories of Swiss mountains and unexpected downpours, reminding us that shared optimism can weather any storm.

Take a moment to breathe in the new morning and listen deeply.

Mood: Reflective, Warm, Transitional, Hopeful
Music genre: Classic Rock, Psychedelic Soul, Pop Rock, Soft Rock
